/-!
# Conjecture 5.39

by P. M. Neumann

Every countable group acts faithfully by automorphisms on some finitely generated
solvable group. The latter group can be chosen to have derived length at most $4$.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«5.39»

/--
Every countable group $H$ has a faithful action by automorphisms on a finitely generated
solvable group $G$; that is, there is an injective group homomorphism
$H \to \operatorname{Aut}(G)$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«5.39» :
    ∀ (H : Type) [Group H] [Countable H],
      ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G), Group.FG G ∧ IsSolvable G ∧
        ∃ φ : H →* MulAut G, Function.Injective φ := by
  sorry

Every countable group $H$ has a faithful action by automorphisms on a finitely generated
solvable group $G$ of derived length at most $4$. In Mathlib's convention, this bound is
`derivedSeries G 4 = ⊥`.
-/

theorem kourovka.«5.39».variants.derived_length_le_four :
    ∀ (H : Type) [Group H] [Countable H],
      ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G), Group.FG G ∧ IsSolvable G ∧
        derivedSeries G 4 = ⊥ ∧ ∃ φ : H →* MulAut G, Function.Injective φ := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«5.39»

/-!
# Conjecture 5.39

by P. M. Neumann

Prove that every countable group can act faithfully as a group of automorphisms of a
finitely generated soluble group (of derived length at most $4$).

A group $H$ acts faithfully as a group of automorphisms of $G$ exactly when there is an
injective group homomorphism $H \to \operatorname{Aut}(G)$, i.e. when $H$ is isomorphic to
a subgroup of $\operatorname{Aut}(G)$.

*References:*
- [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46), problem 5.39.
- P. M. Neumann, *in: Groups–Korea, Pusan, 1988* (Lect. Notes Math. **1398**), Springer,
  Berlin, 1989, 124–139 (background, including the relationship with problem 8.50).
-/

namespace Kourovka.«5.39»

/--
Every countable group $H$ can act faithfully as a group of automorphisms of a finitely
generated soluble group: there is a finitely generated soluble group $G$ and an injective
group homomorphism $H \to \operatorname{Aut}(G)$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«5.39» (H : Type*) [Group H] [Countable H] :
    ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G), Group.FG G ∧ IsSolvable G ∧
      ∃ φ : H →* MulAut G, Function.Injective φ := by
  sorry

/--
Stronger form: every countable group $H$ can act faithfully as a group of automorphisms of a
finitely generated soluble group of derived length at most $4$, i.e. there is a finitely
generated group $G$ with $G^{(4)} = 1$ and an injective group homomorphism
$H \to \operatorname{Aut}(G)$. Here $G^{(0)} = G$ and $G^{(n+1)} = [G^{(n)}, G^{(n)}]$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«5.39».variants.derived_length_le_four (H : Type*) [Group H] [Countable H] :
    ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G), Group.FG G ∧ derivedSeries G 4 = ⊥ ∧
      ∃ φ : H →* MulAut G, Function.Injective φ := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«5.39»

The statement is imperative ('Prove that…'), so it is stated as a direct proposition (no answer(sorry)), per CONTRIBUTING.md. No nontriviality hypothesis on H is imposed; trivial/finite H are included as in the source.
The Neumann 1989 Groups–Korea reference and problem 8.50 are cited in the module docstring as background only; they pose no further formal content.

/-!
# Conjecture 5.39

by P. M. Neumann

Prove that every countable group can act faithfully as a group of automorphisms of a
finitely generated soluble group (of derived length at most $4$).

A group $H$ acts faithfully as a group of automorphisms of $G$ exactly when $H$ embeds
into $\operatorname{Aut}(G)$, i.e. when there is an injective group homomorphism
$H \to \operatorname{Aut}(G)$. The converse direction is trivial: the automorphism
group of a finitely generated group is countable.

For background to this problem, in particular its relationship with problem 8.50, see
P. M. Neumann, *in: Groups–Korea, Pusan, 1988 (Lect. Notes Math.*, **1398**), Springer,
Berlin, 1989, 124–139.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«5.39»

/--
Every countable group $H$ can act faithfully as a group of automorphisms of a finitely
generated soluble group: there is a finitely generated soluble group $G$ and an injective
group homomorphism $H \to \operatorname{Aut}(G)$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«5.39» :
    ∀ (H : Type) [Group H] [Countable H],
      ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G), Group.FG G ∧ IsSolvable G ∧
        ∃ f : H →* MulAut G, Function.Injective f := by
  sorry

of a finitely generated soluble group $G$ of derived length at most $4$, i.e. with
$G^{(4)} = 1$. In Mathlib's convention `derivedSeries G 0 = ⊤`, so this is
`derivedSeries G 4 = ⊥`, which already implies `IsSolvable G`.

        ∃ f : H →* MulAut G, Function.Injective f := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«5.39»
